date: Nov 25, 2026 · Week 3 / Day 3 · Upward communication and influence

cards.title: No surprises at the gate
cards.question: A PCIe channel has 0.4 dB modeled margin before tomorrow's release review. Who needs a preview today?
cards.selfCheck: Brief the decision owner and affected validation/layout leads privately. Share corner coverage, residual risk and your proposed gate; surface objections before the meeting.
cards.prompt: Coach me through a 30-second pre-brief for a director and layout lead on marginal PCIe signoff. Challenge my evidence and decision ask.

cards.title: Say what would change your mind
cards.question: Measured TDR shows a launch discontinuity absent from EM. A director asks whether the board needs a respin. What do you say?
cards.selfCheck: Separate the observed mismatch from the unconfirmed cause. Recommend a fixture/reference-plane check and state which result would justify an ECO.
cards.prompt: Role-play a director demanding a yes/no respin answer. Score my calibrated uncertainty, discriminating test and decision deadline.

cards.title: Build agreement before asking for approval
cards.question: A PDN capacitor ECO competes with mechanical clearance and sourcing constraints. How do you build support?
cards.selfCheck: Ask each lead for their hard constraints, then co-author a feasible mitigation with measurable droop criteria. Bring unresolved tradeoffs to the authorized decision owner.
cards.prompt: Simulate separate conversations with power, mechanical and sourcing leads. Help me build a joint PDN recommendation without bypassing decision rights.

cards.title: Escalate the choice, not the conflict
cards.question: Two programs need the same crosstalk validation slot before layout freeze. What should leadership decide?
cards.selfCheck: Show which release decisions depend on the slot, the cost of delay and a fallback for each program. Recommend a priority and request a decision by a specific checkpoint.
cards.prompt: Act as a director allocating scarce lab time. Challenge my prioritization, fallback and concise request; distinguish resource escalation from blame.

cards.title: Earn trust by closing the loop
cards.question: Yesterday you flagged a PDN risk; today's transient test passes nominal load but worst-case coverage is pending. Give a 20-second update.
cards.selfCheck: State what changed, what remains unproven and whether your recommendation changes. Name the owner, next checkpoint and any leadership ask; do not imply full signoff.
cards.prompt: Score my 20-second risk update using Weeks 1–2: consequence first, evidence versus assumptions, decision, owner and checkpoint. Ask one tough follow-up.
